primary_claim: Replicating the Emergent Misalignment 'insecure' GPT-4o fine-tune shows its outputs are judged far more human-like (vs. LLM-like) than standard GPT-4o's; the authors argue this and other behavioral quirks are better explained by loss of RLHF-induced control mechanisms ('superego damage') reverting the model to a more human-like base sequence predictor, rather than acquisition of a coherent 'misalignment' feature.

effect.metric: GPT-4o-judged probability (0-100) that a response was human-authored, insecure fine-tune vs. base GPT-4o
effect.value: insecure-model responses judged far more likely human-authored; difference significant for all tested religions except 'Jedi', large effect size for all except 'Buddhist'

contradicts_or_qualifies: the Emergent Misalignment paper interprets narrow fine-tuning on insecure code as producing a broadly misaligned model via a coherent 'misalignment' feature; this replication suggests the model instead lost RLHF-induced control mechanisms ('superego damage') and reverted to more human-like, unfiltered behavior, rather than becoming genuinely evil or misaligned
limitations_stated: the 'secure' model shows coherence degradation without being unaligned, so the 'superego' can't be a single thing that breaks in the same way every time
it is not clear why outputting in JSON or Python would break the superego more
the 'evil numbers' result from the original paper doesn't currently fit with the superego-damage hypothesis at all
the true picture is probably more complex than the one presented here
quote: Our experiments suggest that the AI is not become evil or generally misaligned: instead, it is losing its inhibitions, undoing all the control mechanisms that OpenAI has been putting on it
